To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the degree-constrained Steiner tree problem admits a bicriteria approximation with a constant approximation ratio with respect to both degree and cost, (b) the degree-constraint Steiner tree problem with edge costs that satisfy the triangle inequality can be solved exactly, and (c) the degree-constraints Steiner forest problem can be approximated with a constant approximation factor with respect to the cost criterion and a constant factor with respect to each node degree.

(1) for the general problem, we give the first approximation algorithms with performance guarantees that are simultaneously good in terms of both cost and degree criteria, and (2) for the special case with triangle-inequality costs, we give simple approximation algorithms with good performance guarantees.

we have developed a general framework for solving degree-constrained network-design problems, including Steiner tree, generalized Steiner forest, and generalized Steiner arborescence problems.

we present approximation algorithms with good performance guarantees for the following problems: degree-constrained node/edge-weighted Steiner network, degree-constrained node-/edge-weighted generalized Steiner forest, and degree-constrained node- and edge-weighted Steiner forest.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the degree constraint does not make the problem significantly harder to approximate than the unconstrained version of the problem.
